business_problem: CARE's small fundraising, finance, legal, communications, and program teams were stretched across growing workloads and fragmented systems, often repeating research and document work instead of reusing prior work as humanitarian-sector funding contracted.
solution_summary: CARE introduced Claude Enterprise through a pilot across several business units and now uses it for prospect research, proposal and report drafting, editing, grant-data analysis, budgeting, and participant-safety review. Fundraisers created reusable Claude skills to apply the CARE Style Guide, cross-check Salesforce records, and assess proposals; a country office connected skills into a seven-stage funding workflow with a human decision gate. With Claude Cowork, a program colleague combined 31 public datasets into an interactive flood-risk dashboard. Other teams use Claude to consolidate multi-country budgets and scan participant feedback from a database for safeguarding concerns. A Claude API-powered research environment scans news and publications for food, economic, regulatory, and environmental signals. CARE requires human review and keeps sensitive information out of public AI tools unless approved; the page does not detail hosting or storage.

data_flow: Public flood and risk datasets are combined in Claude Cowork into an interactive map. Funding calls, donor rules, past performance, templates, and evidence move through a seven-stage proposal workflow, with humans deciding whether to pursue or submit. Claude also analyzes budget data into a dashboard and flagged-country list for finance review, and scans participant-feedback database responses for possible safeguarding concerns.
integration_points: Public datasets and external evidence libraries
business_outcome: Claude gives CARE's fundraising and program teams more capacity for donor relationships, technical writing, budget review, and safeguarding work. Staff report recurring time savings, while AI-enabled research and mapping made analyses possible that CARE otherwise would have needed consultants to perform.
